The Marianas are situated on the northwest periphery of a broad, weak
circulation, Invest 98W, centered between Satawal and Chuuk Lagoon
near 8N150E. A trade-wind trough extends northward from Invest 98W,
with numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms seen along the axis,
approaching the islands from the east. Scattered showers and 
isolated thunderstorms are expected tonight as the trade-wind trough
shifts westward into the area, supported in part by divergence aloft
associated with an upper-level low and trough. Over the next few
days, model guidance shows most of the showers and thunderstorms 
developing near Tinian and Saipan where the strongest convergence
looks to set up, as Invest 98W slowly meanders westward south of the
islands, and an attendant trough to its northeast moves through the
area. Late this weekend into early next week, a quieter ridging 
pattern looks to move in behind 98W.

Marine/Surf...
Gentle to moderate northeast to east winds will prevail across 
Guam and Rota waters though at least Friday night, and start to 
diminish Saturday as wind direction briefly shifts southeast. For
Saipan and Tinian, winds will be moderate to fresh out of the east
over the next few days with occasional strong gusts Friday as
trade winds briefly surge across the far northern CNMI. Combined 
seas of 6 to 8 feet could briefly increase a foot tonight as the 
highest pulse of the northeasterly swell arrives then, for Tinian
and Saipan waters. Seas look to diminish thereafter as this swell
begins to weaken. Meanwhile, there will be a moderate risk of rip 
currents through the weekend, mainly along north and east facing 
reefs. There will also be moderate risk of lightning through at least
Friday night, mainly for Tinian and Saipan.

Tropical Systems...
Two Invest areas were opened by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center 
(JTWC) today. A weak tropical disturbance is located over the 
northern Marshall Islands near 11N167E, designated Invest 97W by JTWC
as of 1000 AM ChST. Invest 97W is currently rated "low" for 
development, meaning development is unlikely within the next 24
hours. Latest Himawari visible satellite shows broad, patchy cloud 
cover across the region with convection focusing near the center of 
97W. The animated satellite imagery loop, and latest scatterometry 
data this morning, depict a weak, but clearly visible surface 
circulation in the vicinity of Rongelap and Bikini Atolls. Although 
there are several weak circulations across eastern and central 
Micronesia, models favor 97W most for development, with latest 
guidance showing gradual organization over the next few days as it 
remains quasi-stationary, strengthening more this coming weekend as 
it begins to move north. It is too early to say much about the 
eventual strength or track as 97W is a newly-formed system, but it 
will continue to be monitored in the coming days.

To the west, a broad, elongated surface circulation is centered
between Satawal and Chuuk Lagoon near 8N150E, now dubbed Invest 98W
by JTWC. Scattered to numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms 
are seen across the area, mainly within the convergent south to 
southwest flow into the disturbance. Invest 98W looks to remain 
broad and disorganized as it shifts west through the next few days, 
maintaining a generally wetter pattern for Chuuk and the Marianas 
into the end of the week. Invest 98W is also rated "sub-low" by 
JTWC, as it is not expected to develop in the next few days.

If Invest 97W or 98W organize and become rated "low" or higher, 
additional information on these disturbances will be found in 
bulletins issued by JTWC under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
Scattered showers from the monsoon trough will continue through
tonight for Majuro and possibly Pohnpei, but are expected to remain
fairly light with no thunderstorms. Kosrae is seeing dryer conditions
and this is expected to continue for the entire forecast period as
the monsoon trough stays weak and generally to the north. Winds are
becoming light by tomorrow over Pohnpei which may allow for some
scattered island effect showers in the afternoon. Light to gentle
winds over Kosrae will be steady until potentially increasing
slightly to gentle to fresh Saturday. Majuro has the highest winds,
with gentle to moderate winds expected most of the forecast period,
potentially becoming fresh Friday night as the monsoon surge peaks
nearby to the northwest and feeds into the developing Invest 97W.
However, with this system staying north, both Pohnpei and Majuro will
also stay generally dry with isolated showers with the exception of
low-end scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms Friday night 
for Majuro and Sunday for Pohnpei.

For the marine forecast, combined seas of 5 to 6 feet will remain
steady for Pohnpei and Kosrae through the whole forecast period.
